gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.

gaps.sentence: You ___ park here — the police tow cars away every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' expresses a rule you must not break: mustn't park.

gaps.sentence: You ___ told me — I would have kept the evening free!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' plus the participle criticizes something that did not happen: should have told.

gaps.sentence: It was careless of her — she ___ have prepared more thoroughly for the interview.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' criticizes a failure to act properly: should have prepared.

gaps.sentence: You ___ take an umbrella — the forecast says heavy rain all day.
gaps.explanation: 'Should' recommends a sensible action: should take.

gaps.sentence: They left at nine and the journey only takes an hour, so they ___ have arrived by now.
gaps.hint: a certain past completion by now
gaps.explanation: 'Must have' expresses confidence about a past event: must have arrived.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ feed the animals, however much they beg.
gaps.hint: a zoo rule that forbids feeding
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' states a prohibition regardless of temptation: mustn't feed.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.
